req.title: Register form GET
req.statement: The system shall serve a registration form at GET /auth/register.

doc.reasoning: R-FLASKR-002 requires GET /auth/register to return HTTP 2xx with a registration form. Tests cover: (1) positive EP — valid GET returns 200 with form fields present; (2) negative NEG — wrong HTTP method (POST with no data) still returns 200 (render_template path) but a non-existent method like DELETE returns 405; (3) boundary BVA — response body contains exactly the expected HTML landmarks (form action, input names) to catch constant/string mutations; (4) STC — unauthenticated vs authenticated state both reach the register page (no login_required guard); (5) DT — verifying Content-Type header is text/html to catch response-type mutations.

tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_register_get_returns_200():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.get('/auth/register')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert b'register' in r.data.lower()

test_register_get_returns_200()

actions: POST /auth/login with valid credentials to establish session

tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_register_get_authenticated_still_serves_form():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    login_r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'test', 'password': 'test'})
    assert login_r.status_code == 302
    r = client.get('/auth/register')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert b'<form' in r.data

test_register_get_authenticated_still_serves_form()
